requirement: Download a release artifact over HTTP with requests, verifying its SHA-256 and only replacing the destination file once the complete body matches, without leaving partial temp files behind.
skeleton: A chunk size constant, a ChecksumMismatchError, and download streaming into a mkstemp file beside the destination, hashing as it writes, comparing digests case-insensitively, replacing atomically, and deleting the temp file on any error.
caption: Downloading a file with requests so a bad transfer never replaces a good file. ChecksumMismatchError is a plain Exception. download(session, url, dest, *, sha256, timeout=10.0) opens session.get with stream=True and the timeout, calls raise_for_status so an HTTP error raises requests.HTTPError before anything is written, and creates a temp file with tempfile.mkstemp in dest's directory. It streams iter_content chunks of CHUNK_SIZE into the temp file opened in binary mode while updating hashlib.sha256 and a byte count. If the hex digest differs from sha256 compared case-insensitively it raises ChecksumMismatchError; otherwise the temp file replaces dest with Path.replace. Any exception deletes the temp file and re-raises. It returns the size. The fixture asserts, against a local HTTP server, that a matching download lands with only out.bin left, that an uppercase digest is accepted, that a mismatch raises ChecksumMismatchError leaving no file or keeping the previous one, and that a 404 raises requests.HTTPError with nothing written.

plan.intent: Fetch pinned binaries safely in an installer
constraints: HTTP errors raise requests.HTTPError before writing
The body streams into a temp file in the destination directory
A mismatch raises ChecksumMismatchError and leaves dest untouched
The temp file is removed on any failure

rationale.teaches: Stream with iter_content into a sibling temp file, verify the hash before an atomic Path.replace, and clean up on every exception path.
rationale.why: Writing straight to dest or replacing before the check corrupts the good copy, and leftover temp files accumulate on every failed attempt.

ops.docstring: Download a file with requests atomically and verify its checksum.

ops.source:
class ChecksumMismatchError(Exception):
    """Raised when the downloaded bytes do not match the expected digest."""

def download(
    session: requests.Session,
    url: str,
    dest: Path,
    *,
    sha256: str,
    timeout: float = 10.0,
) -> int:
    """Stream ``url`` into ``dest`` only if its SHA-256 matches; return bytes."""
    with session.get(url, stream=True, timeout=timeout) as resp:
        resp.raise_for_status()
        digest = hashlib.sha256()
        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=dest.parent, prefix=f".{dest.name}.")
        tmp = Path(tmp_name)
        try:
            size = 0
            with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as out:
                for chunk in resp.iter_content(chunk_size=CHUNK_SIZE):
                    out.write(chunk)
                    digest.update(chunk)
                    size += len(chunk)
            actual = digest.hexdigest()
            if actual != sha256.lower():
                raise ChecksumMismatchError(f"expected {sha256}, got {actual}")
            tmp.replace(dest)
        except BaseException:
            tmp.unlink(missing_ok=True)
            raise
    return size

candidates.why_wrong: An uppercase expected digest is rejected as a mismatch.
Failed downloads leave hidden temp files in the destination directory.
The file replaces dest before the digest is checked, destroying the previous copy.
A 404 body is hashed and reported as a checksum mismatch instead of HTTPError.
The temp file is opened in text mode, so writing bytes raises TypeError.
